title: The Two Candles
text: Two candles burn before an empty niche, one for the world and one for the self, their flames leaning toward each other. The Six ask which you would keep lit, a monk says. There is wax enough for only one.

options.label: The Empress's child tends the world's candle, giving the wax to others.

outcomes.text: The niche fills with light, and the party is warmed through.

options.label: The Hermit's child tends the self's candle, keeping the wax for their own soul.

outcomes.text: They stand very still, calm for the first time in a long while.

options.label: The Leader snuffs them both; the Six can choose for themselves.

outcomes.text: The dark in the niche looks back. It leaves something behind in the wax.
